name: AL-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by roughly 23 points
Rogers holds an overwhelming fundraising advantage over McInnis
No polls or expert ratings signal any competitiveness
Prediction markets price a Republican win near 97 percent
model.rationale: Alabama's 3rd is a deeply Republican district, and incumbent Mike Rogers pairs that lean with a dominant financial position while Lee McInnis has raised almost nothing. With no polls, no expert attention, and markets firmly favoring Rogers, every available signal points to a decisive Republican win.
model.watch: Only an extraordinary national wave or a major unexpected scandal involving Rogers could put this seat in doubt.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 3rd District is among the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 23 points toward the GOP. Mike Rogers, the longtime incumbent, is seeking another term and has built a commanding financial position, raising about $2.45 million and holding $2.66 million on hand. Democratic nominee Lee McInnis has raised roughly $61,000 with under $10,000 available, leaving little capacity for advertising or outreach.

No public polls or expert ratings track the race, and prediction markets put Republican odds near 97 percent. District lean, incumbency, and the large money gap all point the same direction, and even a favorable national environment for Democrats would need to be historic to close a margin of this size. The seat is rated Safe Republican.
